title: Enhancing Crime Scene Investigations: From Technology to Evidence
abstract: This PhD dissertation investigates how emerging technologies — including 3D reconstruction, depth cameras, LiDAR, thermal and hyperspectral imaging, ground-penetrating radar, electronic noses, and unmanned aerial vehicles — can be integrated into crime scene investigation, from on-scene documentation to courtroom evidence. Drawing on technological evaluations and case studies, it examines how these tools improve the efficiency, safety, and effectiveness of investigations, and analyses the practical barriers to adoption, including high costs, insufficient training, institutional resistance, and the persistent gap between public expectations and actual capabilities. The dissertation outlines a path toward the responsible integration of AI-supported sensing and 3D reconstruction into forensic practice. Defended at the University of Twente on 22 September 2026.
